note: Heroes sourced from Wikimedia Commons for guides that were carrying another slug's image. Uploads go to account #3 (bwppi9gc) per 99_Системное/CLOUDINARY_ROUTING.md.

heroes.why: A Roman daily market with visible per-kilo price cards is the subject of the page, not a monument.
An ordinary Lucca street with shops under lived-in flats. Lucca is a real destination for American relocators to Tuscany.
The comune building is literally where the ufficio di stato civile holds the records a descent claim is built from.
Piazza delle Erbe in Verona with the market up and people crossing it. A liveable city rather than a landmark, and Verona is not claimed by any area page.
Bologna porticoes in daylight with people walking and working. A city you could live in, not a monument shot, which is what the visa is actually about.
Cefalu from the west. A Sicilian coastal town of about 14,000 people, which is to say one that actually qualifies for the 7% pensioner regime the page is built around.

Orvieto at dawn from the Fortezza, over the Umbrian valley. Umbria is a region British buyers actually settle in, and the frame shows the modern town below the historic one rather than only the postcard half.
A Milanese corner block at dusk: exactly the multi-unit building with balconies and ground-floor shops that the condominio rules on this page govern.

heroes.commons: La Spezia, Biassa, sentiero 504 per Sant'Antonio 1.jpg
heroes.why: A made stone path running beside a dry stone boundary wall. Both legal ideas on the page in one frame: the built track that creates an apparent right of way, and the permanent wall that evidences exclusive possession.

heroes.commons: 4107 - Venezia - Palazzo ducale - Colonna 21 - Notarius - Foto Giovanni Dall'Orto, 17-Aug-2006.jpg
heroes.why: A 14th-century capital on the Doge's Palace showing a notary at work with NOTARIVS carved above him. Italian, literally the subject, and it makes the page's point that the notarial function here is centuries old.
An actual Italian cadastral map sheet. The page is about what the catasto records and what it does not, so the register itself is the subject.
An Italian estate agency window. The proposta irrevocabile and the first money change hands here, before any notaio is involved.
The notarial archive in Florence. The page is about what the deed and the registers actually record, so the building that holds them is the subject.
